note: Refractive index of clear glasses. Sellmeier: n² = 1 + Σ Bᵢλ²/(λ² − Cᵢ), λ in µm, coef = [B1, C1, B2, C2, B3, C3] (C in µm²). Cauchy: n = A + Bλ² + C/λ², coef = [A, B, C]. nd and vd are the datasheet values, kept to check the formula against. Coefficients copied from the refractiveindex.info database (CC0), which takes the Schott glasses from the SCHOTT Zemax catalog 2017-01-20b.

glasses.label: fused silica
glasses.about: Silica alone, the network with nothing added. Its curve is the lowest on the chart.

glasses.label: window glass
glasses.about: Clear soda-lime window glass, the glass the studio's batch makes. Soda and lime loosen the silica network and raise the index a little.

glasses.label: N-BK7 crown
glasses.about: The most widely used optical crown: low index, low dispersion.

glasses.label: F2 lead flint
glasses.about: A standard flint, made with lead oxide. It has more lead than tableware lead crystal.

glasses.label: SF11 dense flint
glasses.about: A dense flint with a great deal of lead. Faintly yellow, because its ultraviolet absorption reaches the violet (SCHOTT TIE-35).

glasses.label: N-SF11, lead-free
glasses.about: Schott's lead-free replacement for SF11, with titanium in place of lead. Its index and dispersion are nearly the same.
